questions.stem: Why can water transport many ions and polar molecules through blood plasma and cytoplasm?
options: Its polarity surrounds and separates charged particles
Its molecules are non-polar
It has no intermolecular attractions
It converts every solute into a lipid
questions.explanation: Water is polar. Its partially charged regions form hydration shells around ions and interact with other polar substances, allowing them to remain dispersed in solution.

questions.stem: A storage polysaccharide is completely hydrolysed. Which change is expected in the reaction mixture?
options: Fewer reducing-sugar molecules
More monosaccharide molecules
More peptide bonds
Formation of phospholipid bilayers
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis uses water to break glycosidic bonds, releasing the monosaccharide units from which the polysaccharide was built.

questions.stem: Phospholipids spontaneously form bilayers in water mainly because each molecule:
options: Is made entirely of amino acids
Contains two hydrophilic tails
Has a hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails
Forms covalent bonds with every neighbouring molecule
questions.explanation: The polar heads interact with water while the non-polar fatty-acid tails avoid it. This amphipathic character drives bilayer formation.

questions.stem: A globular protein is heat-denatured without hydrolysis. Which feature is most likely to remain intact?
options: Its precise active-site shape
All hydrogen bonds
Its normal tertiary structure
The amino-acid sequence of each polypeptide
questions.explanation: Denaturation disrupts interactions that maintain secondary and tertiary structure, but it does not normally break the peptide bonds of the primary amino-acid sequence.

questions.stem: In double-stranded DNA, adenine constitutes 28% of the bases. What percentage is cytosine?
questions.explanation: A pairs with T, so A + T = 56%. The remaining 44% is split equally between G and C; cytosine is 22%.

questions.stem: Two otherwise similar phospholipid mixtures differ only in fatty acid tails. Mixture P has more cis double bonds. At the same moderate temperature, P is expected to be:
options: More tightly packed and less fluid
Unable to form a bilayer
Covalently bonded into a rigid network
Less tightly packed and more fluid
questions.explanation: Cis double bonds introduce bends that hinder close packing. This generally increases bilayer fluidity relative to more saturated tails under comparable conditions.
